profile.headline: Electric Drive Software Engineer at General Motors

positions.title: Electric Drive Software Engineer
positions.description: •	Member of a team responsible for developing the HardWare Input/Output (HWIO) C software for a dual-core NXP MPC microprocessor to be used in the upcoming generation of electric-propulsion Electronic Control Units (ECU’s)

positions.title: Software Integration Lead (SWIL), Hybrid Prop. Systems
positions.description:
•	Responsible for the oversight, compiling, linking, and base-level validation of C software for a hybrid-propulsion Electronic Control Unit (ECU). A Unix/Linux-based IBM-Synergy environment, makefiles, link-location files, Perl scripts, and Python scripts were utilized to perform these operations and to generate various build products, including the .ptp flash executable file, used to support downstream software-validation work
•	Worked with the consumers of the software builds (such as in-vehicle calibrators) and various algorithm groups to ensure the software had desirable content. Continuously hand-patched the software to correct behavior as reported by downstream software consumers
•	Diagnosed microprocessor operations using Lauterbach microprocessor debuggers. Such operations included memory (ROM and RAM) layout and management, real-time operating systems, execution throughput, stack utilization, operation integrity (such as exception handling and watch-dog timers), CAN and LIN communications, and more
•	Pursued a side project with a partner to optimally layout the ROM and RAM memory maps for the upcoming Nexus MPC hybrid-propulsion ECU’s. Significant insight into software requirements was necessary
•	Tested the effects that canceling an ECU shutdown had on flash-memory erase and write operations (for long-term data) to ensure that the flash memory did not become Error-Correcting Code (ECC) corrupted. Analysis of the HWIO software used in the erase and write operations and the use of a Lauterbach microprocessor debugger to step through assembly were required
•	Conducted several analyses to determine software quality and communicated with software owners to resolve issues. Example: Wrote a Perl script to check that all real-time operating system Mng() functions defined in the software were indeed scheduled to be executed in a master schedule file
•	Numerous General Motors recognitions received via General Motors’ peer-recognition system

positions.title: Controller Integration Engineer (CIE), Hybrid Prop. Systems
positions.description:
•	Responsible for the high-level validation of C software executing in a hybrid-propulsion ECU while integrated in either a Hardware-In-the-Loop (HIL) environment or in-vehicle. The ECU interfaced the high-DC voltage from high-voltage batteries to three-phase AC voltage to drive propulsion motors
•	Significant Design for Six Sigma (DFSS) team projects in which I took the lead role included emulating end-of-line vehicle testing in a HIL environment and investigating calibration changes to improve the robustness of low-voltage battery diagnostics. The goals set forth in both projects were achieved
•	Used ETAS INCA to measure global objects in the ECU’s RAM to determine if the C software was executing correctly and that the ECU’s hardware-actuator interfaces were operational. Example: Ensured that the ECU’s software was executing AutoStops/Starts (engine disable when vehicle is stopped) correctly by analyzing the torque profiles and statuses of the engine and motor
•	Worked with GM’s Technical Center India (TCI) weekly to validate the ECU’s diagnostic services (issuing special ECU commands and requesting data via CAN communications). Investigated the discovered issues and communicated with the software owners to correct them. Example: Wrote test cases to invoke the numerous reasons that inhibit AutoStops/Starts and confirmed these reasons were communicated correctly over CAN
•	Used Lauterbach microprocessor debuggers to step through assembly and to investigate low-level microprocessor operations. Example: Collaborated with a team to investigate a torque-abatement issue caused by CAN-communication disconnect testing. I connected a Lauterbach to determine that certain RAM global objects were not initialized correctly in the remedial algorithm used to handle CAN-communication loss. We were recognized for our efforts

positions.title: Hands-On Experience
positions.description:
• Took a laboratory-based embedded controls course, a real-time computing course, and a stochastic-controls course during the Fall 2015 quarter
• Member of the Michigan Autonomous Aerial Vehicles (MAAV) Club. Helped develop a MATLAB-based simulation of an extended Kalman filter used to estimate the states of the club's autonomous quad-rotor helicopter
• Aerospace Information Systems (AERO 552), Winter 2015. Involved substantial code development in C++. The final-course team project was to write the upper-level navigation and control software of a quad-rotor helicopter using C software which was compiled and executed on a BeagleBone Black embedded controller with the Linux-Debian kernel. The quad-rotor helicopter flew successfully. Received an A in the course
• Conducted an adaptive-control independent study under Dr. Dennis Bernstein during the Fall 2014 quarter. Was exposed to the principles of adaptive control and ran numerous simulations of a sophisticated adaptive controller under a wide spectrum of plant dynamics. Wrote a detailed report describing the learning experience and the results obtained for which I received an A

positions.title: AVG Final-Line Electrical Intern
positions.description:
• Supported the AVG Group in the transition to the next vehicle electrical architecture 
• Learned about the CAN and Ethernet network-communication protocols and their respective API software
• Wrote routines in C at the API layer to test the next generation of CAN API software to be used in vehicle-assembly verification
• Gained valuable knowledge of the systems and procedures used to certify vehicle electrical-system functionality

positions.title: LabVIEW Control-Systems Engineer
positions.description:
•	Designed a 2000 psi flow-pump with a partner for a water-pressure system
•	SolidWorks software and stress analysis aided the flow-pump design
•	Wrote a LabVIEW program to operate the water-pressure system which included PID compensators
•	Designed a LabVIEW-controlled system to regulate solar-heated water
•	Developed a test apparatus, LabVIEW program, and manual for a centrifuge system 
•	Consistently resolved any issues with LabVIEW code and associated electrical components
•	Daily collaboration with other engineers to develop their systems

positions.title: Mechatronics and Robotics Engineer
positions.description:
•	Worked on a team of four to design, construct, and program an autonomous robot
•	Programmed the robot using LabVIEW and received first-hand experience with system integration
•	My responsibilities included the development and testing of various circuitry boards
•	Each member contributed an average of 40 hours every week to complete the robot
•	Placed 3rd out of 11 teams in the end-of-semester competition

positions.title: PCB-Design Engineer
positions.description:
•	Used Eagle PCB-design software and reverse-engineering to develop gas-concentration measurement circuitry 
•	Communicated with my boss often about the progress of the circuitry development
•	Produced a second circuit prototype to implement improvements upon the first 
•	The measurement circuitry is currently being used by other students to conduct their research

positions.title: Communications Director, Senior Design Project
positions.description:
• Worked on a team of five to design and construct a gas-deposition measurement chamber 
• Contributed to the mechanical aspects of the chamber design and also to the development of the flow system
• Collaborated with the team manager to structure the team's weekly meetings
• Provided frequent progress reports and presentations
• Placed 3rd out of 22 teams at the Senior Design Project Exposition in May 2012

positions.title: Independent Study under Dr. Jean Hertzberg
positions.description:
•	Worked with a partner to build and analyze a jet fuel nozzle system using research literature
•	Wrote a comprehensive technical report to summarize the work done for which we received A’s
•	Nominated for the Outstanding Graduate for Research of the College of Engineering award, Fall 2013

honors.title: Cum Laude
honors.description: My cumulative undergraduate GPA was higher than a 3.70.
honors.issuer: Issued by University of Colorado Boulder · Dec 2013

honors.title: Nominee for the Outstanding Graduate for Research
honors.description: This nomination was awarded for the excellent work that my partner and I completed for our independent study spanning from May to December of 2013.
honors.issuer: Issued by University of Colorado Boulder · Dec 2013
